subject: Using exposed stan functions in R package

messages.author: 29ce8550baceaeb0
messages.subject: Using exposed stan functions in R package
parts:
Hey all (but especially Ben) - 

Is there an easy way of including Stan functions in an R package so that I can compile on installation rather than on loading? 

At the moment I have stan files in exec/ that contain some functions that I want to use in R. I presume these are all being compiled on build, but I don't how to reference the compiled models. I'm using a workaround by running expose_stan_functions(mypackage:::stanmodels$mystanscriptwithfunctions) but then I'm just compiling it again. 

Ideas? 

Jim

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Using exposed stan functions in R package
parts:
On Wednesday, April 6, 2016 at 12:25:00 PM UTC-4, James Savage wrote:
Is there an easy way of including Stan functions in an R package so that I can compile on installation rather than on loading?

I think you would have to call expose_stan_functions() on a .stan file, fish the .cpp file out of tempdir(), and copy it into the src/ directory of your package. Then it is pretty much the same as if you wrote the C++ by hand. Presumably you would have to list Rcpp, RcppEigen, Boost, StanHeaders, etc. after LinkingTo: in the DESCRIPTION file.

Ben
